title: Sounds in Words
goal: Hear that spoken words are made of separate sounds, and blend/segment 2–3-sound words *orally* — no letters yet, except a 60-second preview of two shapes at the very end.
newToday: oral phonemic awareness (blending, segmenting), mouth-position awareness.
time: 15–20 minutes (shorter than later lessons on purpose).

listen.title: A Big Noisy Day
listen.passage: Sam woke up to a loud bang. It was not thunder — it was the neighbor fixing his old truck again! Sam's little sister covered her ears and laughed. "That truck is louder than a drum," she said. Their mother peeked out the window and shook her head. "Every single morning," she sighed, but she was smiling. Outside, the truck coughed, sputtered, and finally started with a satisfying roar. Sam waved at the neighbor, who waved back, covered in oil and grinning proudly.

tier2.def: made short, uneven, coughing sounds (like an engine that won't start smoothly).
tier2.full: made short, uneven, coughing sounds (like an engine that won't start smoothly). "The old car sputtered before it finally started." "The candle sputtered and went out." Your turn: can you think of something else that sputters?

tier2.def: giving a feeling of pleasure because something worked out or finished well.
tier2.full: giving a feeling of pleasure because something worked out or finished well. "It was satisfying to finally fix the leaky tap." "Eating a good meal after a long day feels satisfying." Your turn: tell me one thing that feels satisfying to you.

questions: What was the loud noise, really?
How do you think the mother really felt about the noise — annoyed, amused, both? Why do you think that?
